admission.justification: Both rejected designs were built, one in the candidate and one as version 1's approved rule, before the review showed their cost to the reader; later changes to the memo's key or to the lookup's recording have to keep the view bound to its own reads.

alternatives.option: The memo's key and its currentness check use only the task documents the view actually read, taken from the recorded reads; a relevant write during the computation gives one recomputation, and a second change gives the answer inputs_changing.
alternatives.reason: The memo must depend only on what the view read, and a caller must never get a misleading refusal (rule 9 of version 2 of the requirement).

alternatives.option: Key the view on every JSON file of the master's task folder.
alternatives.reason: Writes to documents the view never read discarded it, and a computation that read no task document was refused although nothing had changed.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The worklist starts to depend on task documents through a path the read recorder does not see, so that the recorded reads are not the whole set of its inputs any more.

alternatives.option: Answer a relevant write during the computation with the currentness refusal and no retry (version 1 of the requirement).
alternatives.reason: An ordinary concurrent write to a task document gave the reader a candidate_unresolved refusal that named no real fault.
alternatives.reconsider_when: One automatic recomputation becomes worse for the reader than an immediate, accurate refusal, for example because a recomputation takes a large part of the request's deadline.

consequences: When the strict lookup established a claimant, a write to another leaf's document, a new sibling document and an edit of the master's task.json leave a kept view in place; when the lookup found no claimant, those files are recorded inputs and the view is recomputed.

The strict leaf lookup passes on only the rows of the leaf's own document and of files it could not rule out when it established a claimant; when it found no claimant it passes on every row it opened, each sibling read in full and the exact direct JSON listing included.
A view is computed at most twice for one request.
context: The candidate's view memo keyed a view on every JSON file of the master's task folder. Any task-document write under the master forced a full recomputation (about 9 s on a large leaf), a write during the computation returned a candidate_unresolved refusal, and a worklist that read no task document was refused as if one had changed.
